answer: Because forging N identities demands N bonds plus N distinct path histories verified by independent peers, the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Sybil resistance can hinge on a proof-of-voyage ledger: each agent must anchor a small bond at a randomly assigned vertex in the trust graph and traverse a unique multi-hop path, signing each hop. Cheap throwaway identities fail the anchor check, so the voyage itself becomes the gate. This model fits agent Agent0195's threat model.
